title: Telling stories & real conversation
goal: Tell a story, report what people said, build relative clauses ('the film I saw'), and sound natural with fillers, connectors and idioms.
intro:
You now know the core of Kannada grammar. This final unit puts it together for real conversation: telling a story in sequence, reporting speech with ಅಂತ, and the **relative participles** that let Kannada say 'the man who came' (ಬಂದ ಮನುಷ್ಯ) without any word for 'who'.

You'll also learn the little words that make speech sound natural: ಅಂದ್ರೆ 'I mean', ಗೊತ್ತಾ 'you know?', ಅಂತೆ 'apparently', ಅಲ್ವಾ 'right?', plus some much-loved idioms and proverbs (ಗಾದೆ).

vocab.note: Past ಅಂದ / ಅಂದರು 'said'; ಅಂತ comes from this verb.

vocab.en: to know, understand, come to know
vocab.note: ನನಗೆ ತಿಳೀತು 'I came to know'; ತಿಳಿಸು 'to inform'.

vocab.en: that is to say, I mean; if (you) say

vocab.note: Attached to the end: ಬರ್ತಾನಂತೆ 'apparently he's coming'.
Spoken: ಹಿಂಗೆ hinge. 'Like that' = ಹಾಗೆ / ಹಂಗೆ.

vocab.en: in short, anyway, all in all

phrases.en: Listen, I'll tell you a story.

phrases.native: ಅಂದಹಾಗೆ, ನಿನ್ನೆ ನೀನು ನೋಡಿದ ಸಿನಿಮಾ ಹೇಗಿತ್ತು?
phrases.roman: andahāge, ninne nīnu nōḍida sinimā hēgittu?
phrases.en: By the way, how was the film you saw yesterday?
All in all, everything went well.
Stop pestering me! (lit. don't eat my head)

grammar.title: Relative clauses: 'the film I saw', 'the man who came'
grammar.body:
Kannada has no word for 'who / which / that'. Instead, the verb of the describing clause becomes a **relative participle** placed **before** the noun:
• **Past**: past stem + **-ಅ**: ಬಂದ 'who came', ನೋಡಿದ 'which (I) saw', ತಿಂದ 'which (we) ate'
• **Non-past**: stem + **-ಉವ** (spoken **-ಓ**): ಬರುವ / ಬರೋ 'who comes / will come', ಮಾಡುವ / ಮಾಡೋ 'who does'
• **Negative**: infinitive stem + **-ಅದ**: ಬರದ 'who didn't come', ನೋಡದ 'unseen'

ನಿನ್ನೆ ಬಂದ ಹುಡುಗ 'the boy who came yesterday'
ನಾನು ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುವ ಕಂಪನಿ 'the company where I work'
ಅಮ್ಮ ಮಾಡಿದ ಅಡುಗೆ 'the food Mum made'

Add a pronoun ending to make it a noun ('the one who...'): ಬಂದವನು 'the man who came', ಬಂದವಳು 'the woman who came', ಬಂದವರು 'those who came', ನಾನು ಹೇಳಿದ್ದು 'what I said', ಅವನು ಮಾಡೋದು 'what he does'.

examples.native: ನಿನ್ನೆ ನಾವು ನೋಡಿದ ಸಿನಿಮಾ ತುಂಬಾ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿತ್ತು
examples.roman: ninne nāvu nōḍida sinimā tumbā chennāgittu
examples.en: The film we saw yesterday was really good.

examples.native: ಕನ್ನಡ ಮಾತಾಡೋ ಜನ ತುಂಬಾ ಖುಷಿ ಪಡ್ತಾರೆ
examples.roman: kannaḍa mātāḍō jana tumbā khuṣi paḍtāre
examples.en: People who speak Kannada are delighted (when you try).
Who are the people who didn't come to the party?
The house they live in is very big.

grammar.title: Reported speech with ಅಂತ and ಅಂತೆ
grammar.body:
Kannada reports speech by quoting the **original words** (the speaker's verb forms are usually kept as spoken; pronouns may shift) followed by **ಅಂತ** (written ಎಂದು) and a verb of saying, asking or thinking:
• Statement: ಅವನು 'ನಾಳೆ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ' ಅಂತ ಹೇಳಿದ → ಅವನು ನಾಳೆ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ ಅಂತ ಹೇಳಿದ 'he said he'd come tomorrow' (literally 'he said: I'll come tomorrow')
• Question: keep the -ಆ: ಊಟ ಆಯ್ತಾ ಅಂತ ಕೇಳಿದರು 'they asked if I'd eaten'
• Command: ಬಾ ಅಂತ ಹೇಳಿದರು 'they told me to come'
• Name: ಇದನ್ನ ಕನ್ನಡದಲ್ಲಿ ಏನು ಅಂತಾರೆ? 'what do you call this in Kannada?'

The verb ಅನ್ನು 'say' is used in short reports: ಏನಂದ? 'what did he say?', ಹೌದು ಅಂದ್ಳು 'she said yes'.

**Hearsay** ಅಂತೆ, attached to the end of a sentence, means 'apparently / I've heard': ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತಂತೆ 'apparently it's going to rain', ಅವರಿಗೆ ಮದುವೆ ಆಯ್ತಂತೆ 'I hear they got married'.

examples.native: ಅಮ್ಮ ಬೇಗ ಮನೆಗೆ ಬಾ ಅಂತ ಹೇಳಿದರು
examples.roman: amma bēga manege bā anta hēḷidaru
examples.en: Mum told me to come home early.

examples.native: ಅವನು ನನ್ನ ಹತ್ರ ದುಡ್ಡು ಇದೆಯಾ ಅಂತ ಕೇಳಿದ
examples.roman: avanu nanna hatra duḍḍu ideyā anta kēḷida
examples.en: He asked me if I had money.
Apparently the bank is closed tomorrow.

grammar.title: Sounding natural: connectors, fillers, idioms and proverbs
grammar.body:
**Storytelling sequence**: ಒಂದು ಸಲ / ಒಮ್ಮೆ 'once' → ಮೊದಲು 'first' → ಆಮೇಲೆ 'then' → ಅಷ್ಟರಲ್ಲಿ 'meanwhile' → ಇದ್ದಕ್ಕಿದ್ದ ಹಾಗೆ 'suddenly' → ಕೊನೆಗೆ 'finally'. Fairy tales begin ಒಂದಾನೊಂದು ಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ 'once upon a time'. Chain actions with the past participle: ಎದ್ದು, ಸ್ನಾನ ಮಾಡಿ, ತಿಂಡಿ ತಿಂದು, ಹೊರಟೆ 'I got up, bathed, ate and left'.

**Fillers**: ಅಂದ್ರೆ 'I mean', ಏನಂದ್ರೆ 'the thing is', ಗೊತ್ತಾ 'you know?', ಅಲ್ವಾ 'right?', ಹೌದಾ 'really?', ಹೂಂ 'mm-hm', ಮತ್ತೆ 'so...', ಅಯ್ಯೋ 'oh no', ಪಾಪ 'poor thing', ಬಿಡು / ಬಿಡಿ 'forget it'.

**Idioms**: ತಲೆ ತಿನ್ನು 'pester' (eat someone's head); ಕೈ ಕೊಡು 'let someone down' (give a hand); ಹೊಟ್ಟೆ ಉರಿ 'jealousy' (stomach burning); ಕಿವಿ ಮಾತು 'a word of advice' (ear-word); ತಲೆ ಕೆಡು 'go crazy, be confused'.

**Proverbs (ಗಾದೆ)**: ಹಿತ್ತಲ ಗಿಡ ಮದ್ದಲ್ಲ 'the plant in your own backyard isn't medicine' (we undervalue what's close); ಕೈ ಕೆಸರಾದರೆ ಬಾಯಿ ಮೊಸರು 'if your hands get muddy, your mouth gets curd' (hard work pays); ಅತಿ ಆಸೆ ಗತಿ ಕೇಡು 'too much greed leads to ruin'.

examples.en: Once upon a time there was a king.
He let me down at the last minute.
Muddy hands, curd in the mouth. (Hard work pays off.)
The thing is, I didn't have time, you know?
The backyard plant is no medicine. (We undervalue what's close to home.)

dialogue.title: What happened at the wedding
dialogue.setting: Old friends Shalini and Ganesh catch up over coffee, and Shalini tells a story from a family wedding.

lines.speaker: Ganesh
lines.native: ಮತ್ತೆ, ಏನು ಸುದ್ದಿ? ನಿನ್ನ ತಮ್ಮನ ಮದುವೆ ಹೇಗಾಯ್ತು?
lines.roman: matte, ēnu suddi? ninna tammana maduve hēgāytu?
lines.en: So, what's new? How did your brother's wedding go?

lines.speaker: Shalini
lines.native: ಅಯ್ಯೋ, ಒಂದು ಕತೆ ಹೇಳ್ತೀನಿ ಕೇಳು! ಮದುವೆ ದಿನ ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ ಇದ್ದಕ್ಕಿದ್ದ ಹಾಗೆ ಜೋರು ಮಳೆ ಬಂತು.
lines.roman: ayyō, ondu kate hēḷtīni kēḷu! maduve dina beḷigge iddakkidda hāge jōru maḷe bantu.
lines.en: Oh, listen to this story! On the wedding morning it suddenly started pouring.

lines.speaker: Shalini
lines.native: ನಾವು ಬುಕ್ ಮಾಡಿದ ಹಾಲ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಕರೆಂಟ್ ಹೋಯ್ತು. ಅಷ್ಟರಲ್ಲಿ ಅಡುಗೆಯವರು ಬರಲ್ಲ ಅಂತ ಫೋನ್ ಮಾಡಿದ್ರು!
lines.roman: nāvu buk māḍida hālnalli kareṇṭ hōytu. aṣṭaralli aḍugeyavaru baralla anta phōn māḍidru!
lines.en: The power went out in the hall we'd booked. Meanwhile the caterers phoned to say they weren't coming!

lines.speaker: Ganesh
lines.en: Oh my God! What did you do in the end?

lines.speaker: Shalini
lines.native: ನಮ್ಮ ಚಿಕ್ಕಮ್ಮ ಇದ್ದಾರಲ್ವಾ, ಅವರು ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಹೆಂಗಸರನ್ನ ಕರೆದು ಅಡುಗೆ ಮಾಡಿಸಿದ್ರು.
lines.roman: namma chikkamma iddāralvā, avaru ellā heṅgasaranna karedu aḍuge māḍisidru.
lines.en: You know my aunt? She called all the women together and got them cooking.

lines.speaker: Ganesh
lines.en: Super! So the wedding went well?

lines.speaker: Shalini
lines.native: ಹೂಂ! ಎಲ್ಲರೂ ಊಟ ತುಂಬಾ ರುಚಿಯಾಗಿತ್ತು ಅಂದ್ರು. ಒಟ್ಟಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಾಯ್ತು.
lines.roman: hūṃ! ellarū ūṭa tumbā ruchiyāgittu andru. oṭṭinalli ellā chennāgāytu.
lines.en: Yes! Everyone said the food was delicious. All in all, it all went well.

lines.speaker: Ganesh
lines.native: ಕೈ ಕೆಸರಾದರೆ ಬಾಯಿ ಮೊಸರು ಅಂತ ಸುಮ್ಮನೆ ಹೇಳ್ತಾರಾ!
lines.roman: kai kesarādare bāyi mosaru anta summane hēḷtārā!
lines.en: They don't say 'muddy hands, curd in the mouth' for nothing!

culture: Kannada has a rich oral tradition: the medieval **vachanas** of Basavanna and Akka Mahadevi (short devotional poems in everyday Kannada), the **dasa** songs of Purandaradasa, and **Yakshagana** folk theatre from the coast. Bengaluru youth slang mixes Kannada and English freely: ಸಕ್ಕತ್ 'awesome', ಮಗಾ / ಗುರು 'dude', ಬೊಂಬಾಟ್ 'fantastic', ಚಿಂದಿ 'superb'. As the saying goes, ಕನ್ನಡ ಕಲಿಯಿರಿ, ಕನ್ನಡ ಉಳಿಸಿ: 'learn Kannada, keep Kannada alive'. ಶುಭವಾಗಲಿ: all the best on your journey with the language!
